sources.source: Akidau, Bradshaw, Chambers, et al. — The Dataflow Model (VLDB 2015)

items.item: Nothing about the unified model is magical: what's computationally impractical in a batch, micro-batch, streaming, or Lambda Architecture system stays impractical, since CPU, RAM, and disk constraints never move.
The paper reserves 'streaming' and 'batch' for execution engines only, not for the shape of unbounded versus bounded data itself — the theoretical basis a shape-first decision card rests on.
A freshness SLO acts as a hard latency floor: any shape whose floor sits above the SLO line is eliminated outright, regardless of tuning.

at.step: Reveal: the decision card, four shapes against the SLO line

items.item: Among the shapes that clear the floor, the decision rule is the cheapest one, not the one with the most headroom — headroom is infrastructure cost, not a free bonus.

at.step: Reveal: of the survivors, the cheapest one wins

items.item: A single question about reprocessing cost can override the cheapest-that-clears rule, since two shapes with the same floor can differ sharply in how expensive it is to redo old output.

at.step: Predict: which shape wins, and what could flip the answer?

items.item: Lambda sits on the hybrid card (two permanent code paths); Kappa sits on the streaming card (replay is the same job, rerun from the retained log).

at.step: Reveal: Lambda, Kappa, and a unified engine, placed on the card

items.item: A unified execution engine's appeal is Kappa's one-code-path property without hand-building the replay logic — it is a maturing pattern, not a settled default.

Lambda's real cost is organizational (two systems' logic kept in sync by people), while Kappa's real cost is a genuine, temporary resource cost (roughly double output storage during a reprocessing run).

at.step: Reveal: the real cost Lambda pays, and the real cost Kappa pays

items.item: A push source's owning team is responsible for delivery and schema; a pull source's owning pipeline is responsible for extraction — the boundary decides who gets paged.

at.step: Reveal: push versus pull, decided at each source

items.item: A pulled source's silent failure (zero new rows) is indistinguishable from a successful, ordinary quiet day at the level of the pull job's own exit status — only a freshness alert catches the difference.

at.step: Predict: does a silent pulled source look different from a quiet day?

items.item: The Dataflow Model frames batch and streaming as two points on one continuous processing model, which is the theoretical basis unified engines implement in practice.
Tightening a freshness SLO from minutes to seconds can eliminate every shape but one, removing any slower fallback and raising the stakes of the reprocessing-cost question this topic opens with.
